thread:
Cheng: quick heads-up — profiler trace from the nightly MoE run shows all-to-all time blowing up when effective batch > 48. attaching the top-line. :eyes:

Cheng: Profiler snippet:
```
all_to_all (token-routing): 38.2 ms
expert-fwd compute: 14.5 ms
KV-cache lookup / gather: 7.9 ms
allreduce (grad/agg): 2.1 ms
peak nvlink bw observed: ~18 GB/s
note: spikes correlate with token-fanout bursts
```

Sam: do we know if the kernel selector switched off the fused attention path? that can change compute vs comm balance a lot. also what dtype/quantization were these runs?

Maria: these were fp16 float32-attn fallback on some shards — we saw a fallback to the slower attention kernel on rank 3 and 6 last night. also KV-cache sizes are uneven because of short/long mix in the batch -> uneven expert fanout.

Alex: can you paste the torch.profiler command you used? want to check whether all-to-all is synchronous on the default stream or issued async so compute can overlap.

Cheng: ran with: `python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc_per_node=8 --nnodes=1 serve_perf_test.py --moe --batch 64 --seq 1024` and profiler flags `--use_torch_profiler` (default config). i think all-to-all was issued inline.

Sam: try this quick experiment: 1) force fused kernel via env var (FORCE_FUSED_ATTENTION=1) 2) enable async alltoall (MOE_ASYNC_A2A=1) 3) cap per-expert fanout at 64 (EXPERT_MAX_FANOUT=64). see if latency tail improves.

Maria: small note — when we cap fanout we change load distribution and may increase local compute, but it should reduce NVLink saturation. also we should verify KV-cache locality: long prefixes have a much hotter KV cache which increases gather size.

Alex: for measuring overlap try this nvprof-style snippet (rough):
```bash
nvprof --print-gpu-trace python serve_perf_test.py ...
# watch for cudaMemcpy/AllToAll start times vs kernel launch times
```

Cheng: ran an adhoc with FORCE_FUSED_ATTENTION=1 + EXPERT_MAX_FANOUT=64 — saw all_to_all drop from 38ms -> 21ms, compute rose 14.5 -> 18.8ms, end-to-end p99 improved ~12%. promising but not a final fix.

Sam: good sign. next check: is NCCL using tree/allreduce vs ring? on our config ring+nvlink for 8 GPUs can be suboptimal for many-to-many. check `NCCL_PROTO` / `NCCL_ALGO` defaults. if we switch to TREE and enable p2p, may reduce hop count.

Maria: i ran per-rank KV cache histogram — ranks 2/3 have 2x more live tokens (hot clients) -> they create heavy outbound fanout. suggests we need routing smoothing or per-rank admission control.

Alex: longer-term: consider kernel-level packing that respects expert topology (pack tensors so that all-to-all size reduces) and smarter batching heuristics that avoid mixing long-prefix and short-prefix requests. immediate: trial the fanout cap + async A2A + NCCL_ALGO=tree.

Cheng: putting together an A/B run plan. volunteers: Maria will run per-rank KV experiments and histogram logs, Sam will test NCCL_ALGO tree vs ring and measure nvlink utilization, Alex will prototype async a2a streams and a gated fanout flag in runtime. i'll run the combined perf runs and collect traces.

infra-bot: deploy started by Cheng on perf-cluster-7 (job id perf-2026-03-18-11). logs will appear in /logs/perf-2026-03-18-11/. :rocket:

Sam: timeline? can we have first results by EOD? if not, rough ETA.

Maria: i can run the KV histograms in 2 hours, then iterate.

Alex: prototype async a2a this afternoon, likely 4-6h to get reliable traces.

Cheng: plan: collect baseline + 3 variants (fanout-cap, fused-ker, async-a2a+tree) and compare p50/p95/p99 and nvlink bw. i’ll post summaries here. assigning followups in the perf doc. :hammer:
